That Layover Life is a free place for repeat travelers and expats to tell the true story of a trip, keep a map of everywhere they have been, and find someone who lives where they are headed next. I'm Nancy. I started it, I read everything that comes in, and I travel with a 35-kilogram Samoyed who believes he runs the place.
Free to join. We're not a gym.

The lounge was in an airport, and the wine was doing what lounge wine does, which is make the next trip look like an excellent idea. I cannot sit through a layover without researching the next trip, and usually the one after that, while the current one is still in progress.

I also like keeping track of where I have been. In some ways this is a travel blog, and what I did not want was the part where a travel blog needs feeding, where you find yourself booking a trip every weekend to keep the thing current. I wanted a space that belongs to the people using it: somewhere to log a trip and share it the way you would on a social platform, without the politics and the negativity that come attached to most of them. So I built that, and then I left the door open.
I swear by the Mark Twain line about travel:
"Travel is fatal to prejudice, bigotry, and narrow-mindedness, and many of our people need it sorely on these accounts."
He wrote that more than 150 years ago and it has not needed an update.

I'm from Portland, Oregon, and I have lived abroad since 2018, in Brazil, Vietnam and Denmark, with Copenhagen as home now. I also kind of lived in Dubai, where I got "stuck" for more than two and a half months on my way from Denmark to Vietnam, which remains the longest layover I have on record. I speak English, Danish and Portuguese.
My country count is on my traveler profile.

Jay and I have run a marathon on every continent, including one inside our Copenhagen apartment during lockdown (recommended to nobody). I have also driven an EV from Copenhagen to Kosovo and back, despite being unable to charge my own phone.
Owning fewer things left more budget for going places (my husband may disagree with the accounting).
When I am not here, I run
Magnus Waffles is about three years old and has opinions. Often confused with a polar bear, seal, or teddy bear. 100% Samoyed.
His country count is on his Paw Passport.

His contributions have included a full perimeter check of a shed in Saxony, the discovery of a baguette in Sofia, and a visit to a dog bakery in Budapest that he considers the cultural high point of Europe. When we camp, he sleeps on top of me like an Arctic weighted blanket.
He is also the reason the Paw Passport exists. If your travel companion has paws, feathers or scales, they get a page of their own and a country count to go with it.

The rules are short. Every story happened, and it happened to the person whose name is on it. We get the facts right first and are funny second, because the joke is only earned by being right. We laugh at ourselves, at our own decisions and at the occasional inanimate object that had it coming, and never at a place or the people who live there.
Hosted or gifted travel is labeled at the top of the story, where you will see it.
True stories from named travelers about specific places, free and with no paywall.
Tick off every country you have been to and watch your map fill in.
Send a story or your photos. It publishes the moment it passes the submission rules, and your byline stays yours.
Or the cat, the ferret, or one extremely well-traveled parrot.
Real places, by the people who
Travel stories from people who have been there, writing about specific places at specific times. The version a friend would tell you, not the one the algorithm edited.

That Layover Life is a travel storytelling platform and community engine for repeat travelers, expats, and anyone who can turn a six-hour connection into a story worth telling. Contributors write, an editor in Copenhagen reads every word, and every submission gets a human review within 48 hours with the byline kept. Free to read, no paywall on the archive.
Five lenses we read the world through
A city and a time window. What to do with the hours nobody plans for.
Travel with your bestie, any species. Real logistics, Magnus supervising.
The paperwork, the charging stops, the border that wanted a form you somehow already had.
The customs nobody writes on the sign.
The trips themselves. Twelve countries in an EV, a W Trek over Christmas, a sea lion who chose chaos.
Pick one. Stay a while. They overlap more than you would think.
The Library is where every published TLL story lives. Travelers writing about specific places at specific times, searchable by country, pillar or contributor.
Stories publish the moment they pass the submission rules. The editor reads every one after, can correct or pull it under the Charter, and never rewrites your voice. Every byline is a real person.
Every story has a named byline. Bylines are open to nomads, expats, press on assignment, and readers who decide one trip is worth writing up.

Each profile shows their countries, cities, states, national parks, marathons, and the stories they've written. Plus their social links (YouTube, TikTok, Substack, Instagram, Vimeo, Twitter) so you can follow them elsewhere.
If your travel companion has paws, feathers, or scales, the Paw Passport is for them. Register your bestie with name, species, breed, and EU pet passport status.

Pets get their own profile. Their own country count. Their EU pet passport details stored privately. They get tagged on stories they came along on. Travel besties of any species: Samoyed, hairless cat, parrot, ferret, whoever's on the road with you.

Share your story is how stories get into the Library. Three short steps: the story (headline, excerpt, body), the details (the place, the photos, who came along), then credit and consent. It publishes the moment it passes the submission rules.

Automated checks cover the mechanics: 300 words or more, your own photo, a place, links that work. Pass them and the story is live. The editor reads it after and can correct or pull it under the Charter.
An interactive world map of every country you have been to. Rose means been there. Cream means not yet. Hover for the name, click through to the story, and watch the counter creep toward 195.

Behind it sits your Passport: every visit in order, with the city, how long you stayed, who came along (pets included) and the stories you wrote from there. Log all 195 and you are officially a Lifer.
Founder · editor · the one who reads every word
Started this with one passport and a Samoyed in an advisory capacity. Runs marathons on every continent, lives in Copenhagen, and reads every story before it goes out.
✓ Every byline is a real person
✓ Free to read, free to publish
✓ Hosted travel labeled at the top, never buried
The trips happened. The opinions are uncut.
The third-act sag has been edited out.
We are not a booking site. We are a magazine, and every story in it happened. Named travelers who got on the plane. Free to join, free to publish, free to keep on the road.
